notice: Clean-export and clean policy. The Bootstrap defines what is GTT-owned; the CLI consumes this policy (gtt-project.sh export-policy resolves it against the project) and never keeps its own exclusion list. `export --clean` creates a separate delivery artifact; `clean` removes GTT from the current project.

static.reason: GTT Engine: scripts, contracts, index, protection registry, session-adapter declarations, GTT documentation, per-project state
The domain governed by GTT: context, ADRs, proposals, backlog, change request, session, freeze marker
Portable agent contract installed by the bootstrap
Preserved original design source of the bootstrap (GTT evidence artifact)

dynamic.reason: GTT-installed ADE overlay files recorded in the ledger (.gtt/ade.json). Directories that merely resemble an ADE's are never matched by name.

clean.creates: a separate delivery artifact; the source project is not modified
clean.requires_confirmation: files of an adopted ADE with no install record, and ledger files modified since install, are listed for the CLI to confirm; they are not excluded silently

clean.removes: the same ownership set, from the current project
plus: derived and per-project state under .gtt/ and gtt-domain/
clean.confirmation: required from the human (CLI lifecycle); the plan is produced by `clean.plan` and removes nothing itself
clean.keeps: the host project's own files, including its own ADE configuration
